notes.title: Unwording is OUT NOW!!
notes.content:
Hi everyone!

I'm happy to announce that after over a year of work, my new game Unwording  is finally out! :)

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1974250/Unwording

The game launches at $4.99, with a 10% discount - so if you've been interested in the game, the best time to get it would be now! It also really helps in getting the game picked up by Steam's algorithm if it's bought (and reviewed!) in the first 24 hours. This would be SUPER helpful and appreciated!

Thank you for all the support - this has been quite a personal game with a lot of learnings from my own life and experiences, and I sincerely hope you like the game and that it resonates with you!

Lastly, below is the launch trailer. And if you need help with anything, or just want to get in touch, drop me a mail at armaan@frostwoodinteractive.com

notes.title: v1.1.5 - Full gamepad support
notes.content:
Hi!

This latest patch adds full gamepad support for all types of gamepads for Windows and  Linux, expanding from only supporting X360 controllers for Windows.

Also:

1. Fixed an issue where some hotspots wouldn't highlight correctly when controlling Chris with a gamepad.

2. Added a tutorial for cycling hotspots when using gamepad.


Note that the Mac version currently has issues that have temporarily forced it to remain at v1.1.0.  Read more here

- Armaan

notes.title: Fixes in v 1.1.4
notes.content:
Hi

Here are the fixes in v1.1.4:

1. Fixed an issue where the player and NPCs would fall through the ground in the Main Street.

2. Fixed an issue with Chris' outfits.

3. Fixed issues with pathfinding.

Let me know if you run into any other issues! 

-Armaan

notes.title: Fixes in v1.1.3
notes.content:
Hi!

Here are the improvements and fixes for v1.1.3


 Improved hotspot detection when using controllers. The correct interact-able objects will now be highlighted when the player stands in front of them (similar to how it was in the demo)

 Fixed an issue where interact-able objects wouldn't highlight correctly when playing as Chris while using a controller.



Note that only Windows and Linux versions have been updated to v1.1.3, as the Mac version currently has issues that have temporarily forced it to be rolled back to v1.1.0. Read more here

notes.title: v1.1.1 - Gamepad support + fixes in v1.1.2
notes.content:
Hi

The latest update with gamepad support is up now! Enable this and check out the new control schemes by going into the options menu in-game. Note that only Xbox controllers on Windows (update: Only Xbox 360 controllers) are officially supported at the moment, and that other controllers may have unexpected issues. Support for all controllers will be added soon.

Edit: Until then, you could try changing the controls from the launcher before the game starts.

https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31643443/ee3e0d509fcdaa57425a255e8b757b27928c515c.png

The current configuration is this, and might come in handy when customizing the controls - 

https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31643443/825a231ec28fbd8107075e5a7b1e076b43332bdf.png

Fixes in v1.1.2 -
1. Fixed an issue with gamepad compatibility for the combination lock on day 5.
2. Fixed an issue where entering the outfit menu more than once would cause it to become un-highlighted when using the gamepad.

-Armaan

notes.title: New controls, improvements and bug fixes in v1.1.0
notes.content:
Hi!

Firstly, this update contains the long awaited new control scheme for mouse and keyboard, as described in this post: https://steamcommunity.com/games/772290/announcements/detail/3227296324759282710

Also, some people had a hard time navigating around Pineview, so I've added indicators that direct you to your next location and tell you which side-road leads to what destination! You can see a preview of that here:

https://twitter.com/Rainswept_Game/status/1097536757929668608

Apart from these features, the following bugs have been fixed in this update:

1. Fixed the bugged NPC Anav and added him back into the game.
2. Fixed main and pause menu scaling on non-16:9 aspect ratio resolutions.
3. Fixed William not animating when walking outside past the cafe on day 4.
4. Fixed [spoiler]star clusters particles[/spoiler] not triggering correctly on day 5. 
5. Fixed some characters clipping when walking across each other during free roam.
6. Fixed an issue where skipping the end game credits would cause the credits scene to start again before quitting to the main menu.
7. Fixed an issue where you could talk to Chad all over again on day 4.

Now I'm beginning work on adding controller support, and this will likely be added in the next update which should be up in the next couple of days.

Thanks for playing and supporting the game!

-Armaan

notes.title: New controls preview
notes.content:
Hi! 

Here's a preview of the new controls that will be implemented in the next patch -

https://youtu.be/dxo38hsUzO4

Now all visible objects in a scene can be looked at with the cursor without moving up right next to them. Movement is still restricted to the keyboard. It'd be nice to be able to give an option of both mouse and keyboard, but it'd create way too many issues, mostly with pathfinding. 

Also, this scheme means I can possibly start looking at controller support now as well - with cursor movement bound to the right stick. What do you think? Does this fix most of the issues with the controls? Would love to know your opinions!

- Armaan

notes.title: Upcoming controls overhaul + Bugs fixed in v1.0.13b
notes.content:
Hi! 

Before getting to the bug fixes, I wanted to announce that I'm currently trying to figure out a reworked control scheme. Many people have suggested they'd rather the game was completely playable by mouse alone. 

My assumption was that WASD movement feels more immersive as it's something we're used to from third person/ first person action games, but it's quite obvious I was wrong! I'm not 100% sure this will work with the way the game is designed, but it's something I'll work on and let you know about it soon.

Controller support will also be worked on. It's something I've wanted to add from the beginning, but a few issues have prevented its implementation. 

Here's a list of the latest bug fixes and improvements:

1. Added Vsync.
2. Removed the bugged NPC Anav from Central Street.
3. Fixed a bug where it was possible to get stuck in a conversation with Brad during the second conversation.
4. Fixed a bug where interaction with a phone on day 6 was sometimes disabled.
5. Fixed an issue where sometimes Chris could appear in place of Michael in the Main Street after a particular flashback.

-Armaan

 Fixed a rare bug where the conversation options led to wrong answers during the second interview with Brad.

 Fixed a rare bug where it was possible for the player to get stuck on day 5 on the way to the church after talking to Jack.


Let me know of more issues on the discord server here: https://discord.gg/Nwe5ePT

Let me know if you run into any issues in the discord server here:

notes.title: Known issues and Steam Cloud saves
notes.content:
Hi everyone! 

Hope you are having a good time with Rainswept, and thank you for the wonderful response to the game! 

That said, there are some issues that have been pointed out and I'm working on. At the moment they seem to be relatively rare, but if you've encountered them, do let me know in the comments for this post!

1. Loading a saved game disables the ability to turn pages in the journal. (Fixed in v1.0.11a)

2. In some cases the character will always run to the left automatically when not controlled by the player, possibly due to the default joystick controls. A patch for this will be up today. (Fixed in v1.0.11a)

3. It is possible to get stuck in Allan's basement on day 5 after completing the tasks inside the basement. (Fixed in v1.0.11a)

4. Sometimes loading a save will force the player to get stuck in a conversation loop.

5. Framerate cap will be added

Also, Steam Cloud save support has been added for both Windows and Mac. Do let me know if you run into any trouble with this!

-Armaan

notes.title: Bug fixed in v1.0.10
notes.content:
Hi!

This update includes fixes for the following issues:

1. Grandpa couldn't be interacted with on day 5
2. In the cafe on day 4, sometimes the interact option would get stuck on the skater character walking outside the cafe
3. The layers for Officer Blunt and a character in Aspen Street clashed.

Improvements:

1. Shadow added under text in the pause menu.

notes.content:
Hello!

This update fixes a couple of major issues that were spotted in the review copy for the game.

1. Fixed an issue where the player was unable to interact with Allan on Day 4.
2. Added pillarboxing/ letterboxing for monitors with non-16:9 aspect ratios.

notes.title: #20 Update speech bubbles, dialog boxes and diary.
notes.content:
Hi!

These past few weeks I’ve spent most of my time creating the diary system and adding notes for it, but the most exciting news are the new speech bubbles!

https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31643443/48d72b3e0292a1872e98708e096ddcf972ffec41.png

The biggest complaint with the demo was that at times it was hard to tell who was the speaker of which dialogue, as the old speech bubbles were just boxes on top of multiple characters’ heads. I always wanted to add comic style speech bubbles with arrows pointing to the speakers heads, but I wasn’t sure how to make that work dynamically.

The solution was surprisingly simple and only took me a few minutes to implement. All I had to do was make an arrow shaped sprite show up right above the speaking character’s head, disconnected from the dialog box itself. This allows the arrow to follow the character to the edge of the screen while the dialog box remains static - giving it that dynamic look I wanted!

https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31643443/1d10c6cfa65cd6a1516ecb0445187b6950712270.png
Also updated, the conversation options box’s design. What do you think? Would a more solid, black box with red/ blue color text (like in the speech bubbles) work better?

I've also been testing different color combinations for the interaction wheel UI. After a lot of testing and asking for opinions, I've settled on C. What do you think?

https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31643443/419e7462ce1fa70ea7ee40801330acdbaf16e310.png

Lastly, the diary system. This has probably been one of the most time consuming features of all, but it’s hard to imagine a Detective game without a notepad, right? As a result, this feature has been reduced in scope and is a very simplistic record of the Detective’s observations (rather than a multi-tabbed compendium as planned earlier)

https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31643443/99e802177373d0e90cb4e14f99d5de6ef2a4bf8c.png

I think it does the job all the same! It’s still a work in progress, and there are some issues to be sorted out still.
It’ll also contain the map, which I don’t want to reveal yet :)

Another cool feature: A lockpicking minigame!
Gif: https://twitter.com/Rainswept_Game/status/1051153935656935424


A couple more UI and diary improvements to come during the rest of the month, and a bit of work on polishing the dialogues.

See you next time!
Armaan

notes.content:
Hello!

The past few weeks I've been working on adding new locations, story bits and new systems to play with. I've been playing around with ideas to allow players to do a bit more gameplay wise, and this involves the ability to pick and move objects about. Here's a preview of this using puppies as placeholders (cause, why not?)

See the gif here: https://imgur.com/SEjhXuJ

Yes the puppy(s) will feature in the game as well. 

As for new locations, here's where the detective will stay for the duration of the investigation. It's still a work in progress, and I can't wait to get it done! 

https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31643443/190d8855f2ec867a92208795d0da0a1e5a571b8a.jpg

Plotting out the surrounding areas

https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31643443/c8e7edafe2fb801785766bac082fb9b59150a84a.jpg

Added some color!

The woods around Pineview are a major part of the town's identity, so here's a look at the atmosphere within them:

https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31643443/08a061eb213fb563112aebddddcf7bc232703b15.png

We're making speedy progress, let's keep moving!

See you next time

-Armaan

notes.title: Response to the demo, and the release of an updated version!
notes.content:
Hi everyone!

I launched the demo for Rainswept on 2 January on itch.io, and the response has been much more positive  than I could've expected! It's really encouraging that so many people have played and loved the game, and for that, thank you!

It's also been pretty wild (and I must admit, a bit nerve wracking) seeing Youtubers upload let's-play videos of the game. Seeing people play the game and react to its moments has been quite surreal, and encouraging.


An updated demo, based on player feedback, has been released on itch.io and gamejolt, and it now includes a Mac build!

Some of the issues that have been fixed in the updated demo are:



 Speech bubbles - Speech bubbles are now colored! Many people found it confusing to identify the speaker of some dialogues, especially when characters stood close to each other. This is still a temporary solution, just for the demo (as the speech system will be overhauled for the full release) but it should do the job for now.


 Dialogue skipping - You can now skip dialogues by pressing Space/ LB! This is only applicable for those dialogues that the player has already heard at least once before. This will make the market section easier, in case you mistakenly end up asking an NPC the same question you'd already asked before. For the full version, the whole speech bubble will be recreated from scratch, with animations and comic-style arrows pointing to the speaker.


 Fixed some collision bugs - Preventing the player from walking off the scene, and from pushing other NPCs around.


 Made the investigation scene in the kitchen a little less cramped up.


 Fixed the main menu - and gave it some new, fancy effects! The camera now moves down when loading the options, or when starting the game. Cool, huh? ;)


 Loading/ Saving - Added manual saving/loading and save slots.


 Slightly more fleshed out negative dialogue choices when conversing with the local cops.



For the full game, expect improvements on the following:



 Better control schemes - Got a lot of feedback on this! I'll look to change the control scheme to something more comfortable, and allow the player to re-bind keys. If feasible, I shall also consider providing an option between the current "direct" controls and an optional point and click control method.

 Better characters and animations - Another point that received a lot of feedback. Mainly this means more polished character animations, small improvements on art and detail and maybe more detailed eyes and multiple expressions - to replace the current blank stare.

 Overall Improved visuals - Some of the colors don't work perfectly with each other, and this will be improved on. I'm also working on new lighting techniques, to give a better, softer "glow effect". The progress with this shall be shared here!

 Gameplay - I will look to provide more opportunities to engage with the game in a more "traditional" manner. Which means a larger number of, and relatively more complex puzzles than were seen in the demo, and a couple of new mechanics such as a diary/ journal system. I'll also look to integrate the clues picked up during the story into the diary system, which can help the player keep a track of the facts related to the case and help them form their own conclusion before Detective Anderson himself!

 Agency over locations/ movement in the world - In the demo, the player gets carried from one location to the next for each scene in the story. For the full version, I'll look to provide the player with the option to choose from one of the few available scenes/ location for each day's investigation. This will require me to work out the plot to accommodate all choices of the order of locations visited, so the scope of this mechanic is still undecided.



Expect to see more locations, and of course, the full story!

Hope you enjoy the demo! Keep an eye out for weekly updates, and don't forget to wishlist the game on Steam!
